title: Commemorating 200 Years of the Singapore Police Force
what_it_is: Commemorating 200 Years of the Singapore Police Force

sections.label: SPF force size and composition
sections.summary: SPF has grown to a force of 45,000 regular officers, full-time National Servicemen, civilian officers, volunteers and operationally-ready National Servicemen.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: SPF has grown to a force of 45,000 regular officers, full-time National Servicemen, civilian officers, volunteers and operationally-ready National Servicemen.

sections.label: Riot Squad formed after 1952 riots
sections.summary: In 1952, after the Maria Hertogh riots, the Riot Squad, now the Special Operations Command, was formed to respond more effectively to public order incidents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: For example, in 1952, after the Maria Hertogh riots, the Riot Squad in SPF – now known as the Special Operations Command – was formed so that it can respond more effectively to public order incidents.

sections.label: Anti-Scam Centre established in 2019
sections.summary: SPF established the Anti-Scam Centre in 2019 to work with banks, telephone companies and online marketplaces to disrupt scammers and mitigate victims' monetary losses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: For example, SPF established the Anti-Scam Centre in 2019 to work with stakeholders, such as banks, telephone companies and online marketplaces to disrupt scammers' operations and mitigate victims' monetary losses.

sections.label: Officers deployed for historic Summit
sections.summary: More than 6,900 SPF officers were deployed over three days to ensure the historic Summit proceeded smoothly without incident.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: More than 6,900 SPF officers were deployed over a span of three days to ensure that the historic Summit proceeded smoothly without incident.

sections.label: INTERPOL Global Complex hosted in 2015
sections.summary: In 2015, Singapore earned the honour of hosting the INTERPOL Global Complex for Innovation, through which SPF collaborates with foreign law enforcement counterparts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: In 2015, Singapore earned the honour of hosting the INTERPOL Global Complex for Innovation, through which SPF collaborates with foreign law enforcement counterparts on cross-border crimes and the sharing of knowledge, intelligence and best practices.

sections.label: SPF and safe city
sections.summary: Thanks to SPF, our people are able to live, work and play in, arguably, the safest city in the world.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Thanks to SPF, our people are able to live, work and play in, arguably, the safest city in the world.

sections.label: Commemorative award for Police officers
sections.summary: The speaker suggests MHA and SPF consider introducing a commemorative award for Police officers to mark SPF's 200th anniversary and recognise officers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: To commemorate SPF's 200th anniversary and to accord recognition to SPF officers, I would like to suggest that MHA and SPF consider introducing a commemorative award for Police officers.

sections.label: Appreciation for Singapore Police Force
sections.summary: The speaker invites the House to show appreciation and support for the men and women of the Singapore Police Force.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: What always strikes me are the officers' commitment to their mission and their unwavering loyalty to Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Therefore, in conclusion, Madam, may I invite this House to show our sincere appreciation to and strong support for our men and women in the Singapore Police Force.

sections.label: Cumulative years of service
sections.summary: The speaker calculated that between them, the officers served 1,040 years cumulatively.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Between them, they served, and I calculated this, 1,040 years cumulatively.

sections.label: Police Gallantry Medal for Mr Low
sections.summary: President Sheares conferred the Police Gallantry Medal on Mr Low for his bravery.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: For his bravery, President Sheares conferred on Mr Low the Police Gallantry Medal.

sections.label: Bomb planted at railway tracks
sections.summary: A communist sympathiser was planting a homemade bomb at the railway tracks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: What was happening was that a communist sympathiser was planting a homemade bomb at the railway tracks.

sections.label: Officers killed in line of duty
sections.summary: Based on these records, 125 officers have been killed in the line of duty to date.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Based on these records, 125 officers have been killed in the line of duty to date.

sections.label: Inspector Lim Geylang operation
sections.summary: On 5 August 1965, Inspector Lim co-led a pre-dawn operation against a gangster and his men in Geylang, and died at 28 from gun fight wounds.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: On 5 August 1965, Inspector Lim co-led a pre-dawn operation to capture a notorious gangster and his men who were responsible for several kidnappings in Siang Lim Park at Geylang.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: Inspector Lim perished from the wounds he suffered in the gun fight at the age of only 28.

sections.label: Officer killed at Newton Road
sections.summary: The speaker says that in November last year he spoke about the case of a 47-year-old killed in 1994 by an axe-wielding person at Newton Road.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: In November last year, I spoke in this House about his case.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: I related how, at the age of 47 in 1994, he was killed in the line of duty by an axe-wielding person at Newton Road.

sections.label: Police Heritage Centre gallery
sections.summary: The Commemorative Gallery at the Police Heritage Centre was created as a permanent tribute to them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: The Commemorative Gallery at the Police Heritage Centre was created as a permanent tribute to them.

sections.label: Speaker's six years in SPF
sections.summary: The speaker says six years left a lasting impression, with four spent in the STAR unit, and worked and trained with officers in STAR and specialist units.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: As someone fresh from school, these six years have left a lasting impression on my life, my values and impacted me in more ways than one.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: I spent four of these six years with the Special Tactics and Rescue or STAR unit, a little known and highly secretive and clandestine unit within the SPF's Special Operations Command.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: During my service with the STAR unit, I had the honour to work and train with officers in the STAR unit, and almost all the specialist units within SPF.

sections.label: Thanks to SPF specialist units
sections.summary: The speaker recalls hunting criminals and thanks past and present officers of SPF specialist units, naming the Special Operations Command, ang chia, STAR, K-9 and others.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: I recall those memorable days when he hunted down the criminals, and my team and I had to storm and arrest the criminals.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: This draws me to then appreciate and thank all the past and present officers who have served in our specialist units within SPF, from officers of the Special Operations Command, such as those in the well-known red-coloured vehicles colloquially known as the "ang chia", including the STAR unit which handles high-risk and highly armed criminals and criminal hostage situations, and the little known but important SPF K-9 unit to provide specialised capabilities for a whole host of tracking, detection and support to prevent and detect crime.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Other specialist units to make special mention are the Police Security Command, Police Coast Guard, Protective Security Command, Operations Command Centre, Public Transport Security Command, Airport Police, Traffic Police, Training Command, School of Criminal Investigation and the Gurkha contingent.

sections.label: Police community engagement and digitalisation
sections.summary: The Police responds to crime, accidents and incidents with community engagement and partnership, and has reinvented and innovated to keep pace with online crimes and scams.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: With strong community engagement and partnership, the Police has responded to various incidents from crime cases to handling major accidents and incidents to keep the peace in our towns and estates.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: They also partner with the grassroots and community to effectively prevent and detect crime.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: These days, with a more digitalised and virtual operating environment, SPF has also reinvented and innovated to keep pace with new forms of online crimes and scams.

sections.label: CNB, ICA, Prison Service duties
sections.summary: CNB handles high-stakes death penalty cases and crime syndicates, ICA prevents undesirable foreigners' entry, and Prison Service handles offenders' custody, rehabilitation and reintegration.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: CNB is often engaged in very high stakes and dangerous operations, where the offences involve the death penalty and having to battle crime syndicates with significant resources.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Another example is the Immigration and Checkpoints Authority, whose officers are tasked with preventing the entry of undesirable foreigners.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Yet another is the Prison Service, which is charged with the safe custody of offenders, their rehabilitation and their re-integration into society.

sections.label: Police Service Pledge victim updates
sections.summary: The Police Service Pledge requires officers to give victims an interim update within seven days of reporting a case.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: For instance, the Police Service Pledge requires officers to give victims an interim update within seven days of reporting a case.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Where offenders are charged in Court, victims may be heard in certain cases through the use of Victim Impact Statements, and there are higher chances of them receiving compensation from offenders at the time of sentencing.

sections.label: River Valley High School murder training
sections.summary: The River Valley High School murder raises the question of whether every frontline officer is adequately trained to handle traumatised victims and minors.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: More recently, the murder that took place at River Valley High School makes me wonder if every frontline officer has been adequately trained in the people-to-people skills necessary to handle traumatised victims and, in particular, minors.

sections.label: Safety not only metric
sections.summary: Safety must not be the only metric for judging law enforcement agencies; doing justice and acting fairly are equally critical.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In addition and, more importantly, we must never think that safety is the only metric by which to judge the quality of law enforcement agencies.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The need to do justice and to act fairly is equally critical.

sections.label: Public security and anti-terrorism efforts
sections.summary: Efforts have expanded in public security and anti-terrorism, and cyber crimes and online scamming have taken up SPF officers' attention.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: In recent years, much efforts have also been expanded in the area of public security and anti-terrorism.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Cyber crimes and online scamming have also taken up much attention of our SPF officers.

sections.label: COVID-19 period police disputes
sections.summary: During COVID-19, with circuit breaker and work-from-home, Police officers probably contend with more neighbour disputes and complaints on safe distancing breaches.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: During the COVID-19 period, with circuit breaker and work-from-home, Police officers probably have to contend with more cases of neighbours' disputes and complaints on the breach of safe distancing or other prevailing restrictions by groups of people hanging out in our common spaces such as void decks, ball courts, sitting areas or neighbourhood parks.

sections.label: Technology and population constraints
sections.summary: Using different technologies helps make up for constraints in an era of declining birth rates and population.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: The use of different technologies is one way of making up for such constraints in an era of declining birth rates and population.

sections.label: Women officers in SPF
sections.summary: SPF has close to 2,000 women officers, many in leadership positions, commanding specialist units and leading departments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: Today, we have close to 2,000 women officers in SPF, with many serving in leadership positions, taking command of specialist units and leading crucial staff and operational departments.

sections.label: Volunteer Special Constabulary scheme
sections.summary: The VSC was formed in 1946 with 150 volunteers and has grown to over 1,000 volunteer Police officers supporting SPF.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: The Volunteer Special Constabulary (VSC) scheme was formed in 1946 to augment the ranks of regular Police officers after the end of World War II.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: It started with only 150 volunteers and the VSC has since grown to over 1,000 volunteer Police officers, supporting SPF in various operational roles.

sections.label: Singapore law and order ranking
sections.summary: The Gallup 2020 report ranked Singapore top for public perceptions of law and order for the sixth year, with 97% feeling safe at night.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: According to the Gallup 2020 Global Law and Order Report, Singapore has topped an index of public perceptions of law and order for the sixth year in a row.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: An extraordinary 97% of us feel safe walking alone at night, an activity that cannot be taken for granted in many countries.

sections.label: Confidence in SPF
sections.summary: A 2020 IPS survey found 87% confident in SPF, the highest globally, and the Police must safeguard Singaporeans' trust.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: A 2020 survey conducted by the Institute of Policy Studies also found that 87% of respondents were confident or very confident with SPF, the highest level of confidence in police globally.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: Malicious actors have and will continue to engage in efforts to damage the image and credibility of SPF.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: Policing work is no longer just about fighting crimes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: The Police must do all it can to always safeguard the trust that Singaporeans have placed on our men and women in blue.

sections.label: Neighbourhood Police Post system
sections.summary: Lee Kuan Yew tasked Goh Keng Swee to review policing, resulting in the Neighbourhood Police Post system modelled after the Japanese Koban.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Our founding Prime Minister, Mr Lee Kuan Yew had tasked Dr Goh Keng Swee to review our policing approach to keep up with the times.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: The result was one of the most significant changes in policing strategy, where we adopted the Neighbourhood Police Post system, modelled after the Japanese Koban system.

sections.label: Punishment for serious crimes
sections.summary: The Government enhanced punishment for crimes like drug trafficking, armed robbery and kidnapping, with strict minimum sentences and the death penalty.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: At the same time, the Government was also enhancing punishment for some crimes.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We had strict minimum sentences and death penalty for offences like trafficking of drugs above a certain quantity, robbery with firearms and kidnapping.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: The message was simple: in Singapore, crime does not pay.

sections.label: NPP system main insight
sections.summary: The main insight of the NPP system, part of community policing, is that 99% or more of the public are law-abiding.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: In fact, the main insight of our NPP system, which is part of the broader community policing approach is this: 99% or more of the public are law-abiding.

sections.label: Public help solving crime
sections.summary: About 30% of crime was solved with public help then, and the ratio remains between 20% and 30% today.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: In fact, about 30% of our crime then was solved with the help of the public.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Today, I am glad that this ratio remains high, between 20% and 30%, even as our policing capabilities have risen.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Mr Christopher de Souza's recount of the journey of the Police over the 200 years has one key element: that we must constantly adapt and innovate.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: So, I am glad that Minister Shanmugam has set up the HTX – the Home Team Science and Technology Agency – to invest in building new capabilities, especially in the digital area, while Commissioner Hoong Wee Teck is building the frontline capabilities of officers to tackle new and complex crimes, including those in cyberspace.

sections.label: SPF growth since 1820
sections.summary: SPF started as a 12-men team in 1820 and is today a 45,000-strong force.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: SPF started as a 12-men team in 1820.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: It is today a 45,000-strong force with regular Police officers, full-time National Servicemen (NSmen) and supported by civilian officers who are NSmen and volunteers.

sections.label: Gallup Report 2020 safety
sections.summary: The latest Gallup Report 2020 shows 97% of residents in Singapore feel safe walking alone in their neighbourhoods at night.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: Mr Melvin Yong referred to the latest Gallup Report 2020 which shows that 97% of residents in Singapore feel safe when they are walking alone in their neighbourhoods at night.

sections.label: IPS study confidence in SPF
sections.summary: The latest 2020 Institute of Policy Studies study shows 87% of respondents were confident or very confident in SPF.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: The latest 2020 Institute of Policy Studies (IPS) study shows that 87% of respondents were confident or very confident in SPF.

sections.label: Adverse inference for omitted defence
sections.summary: Laws were changed to let Courts draw an adverse inference if an accused raises a defence not mentioned when first interviewed by Police.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: That helped create a framework for the Police to be effective.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: We changed our laws, for example, to allow the Courts to draw an adverse inference if an accused person puts up a defence that he did not mention when he was first interviewed by the Police.

sections.label: 1976 change to right to silence
sections.summary: A major 1976 change requires accused persons to tell Police the truth when interviewed, or adverse inferences can be drawn.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: It runs against a basic principle, some might say, the golden thread, as it were, of the right to remain silent.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: But we made the major change in 1976.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Accused persons have to tell the Police the truth when interviewed, or adverse inferences can be drawn.

sections.label: Packer's due process and crime control models
sections.summary: The passage lists due process features and notes Professor Herbert Packer's 1964 paper describing due process and crime control models.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: If we had not taken this path in 1976, neither the Police nor Singapore would have today's crime control system.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: This meant that (a) the prosecution must prove every ingredient of the offence against the accused beyond a reasonable doubt; (b) the accused had the right to remain silent at any stage of  the criminal justice process, from investigation to trial; (c) the accused had the right not to incriminate himself, except in restricted circumstances; (d) the accused's statements to the police were not admissible except in restricted circumstances; (e) he had the right to give an unsworn statement from the dock; (f) all evidence, even if true, was not admissible if it might have a prejudicial effect on the jury; and (g) the practice of the courts was to require strict compliance with the rules of evidence and procedure and (h) to have strict oversight of jury directions on accomplice evidence and corroboration.” “In a paper published in 1964 on the criminal justice process in the USA, Professor Herbert Packer of Stanford University described two models of criminal justice process, namely, due process and crime control.

sections.label: Packer's crime control model factors
sections.summary: The passage sets out crime control model factors, including presuming guilt after arrest and charging, and discovering factual guilt.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: If the police make an arrest and a prosecutor files criminal charges, the accused should be presumed guilty because the fact-finding of police and prosecutors is highly reliable." I am setting these out, I am not saying that I agree with them.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: This is what Prof Packer had identified. "The main objective of the criminal justice process should be to discover the truth or to establish the factual guilt of the accused." And he has a few other factors too. "The 1976 amendments introduced many features of the crime control model.

sections.label: Chief Justice Chan's two changes
sections.summary: Chief Justice Chan set out two changes: accused statements to police became admissible, and accused lost the right to make an unsworn dock statement.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Chief Justice Chan, as he was, set out the two major changes. “All statements made by an accused to a police officer in the course of investigation would be admissible in evidence… And second, the trial process.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: If the accused is called upon to enter his defence, he has no right to make an unsworn statement from the dock." “These two broad changes led to an increase in the conviction of the factually guilty through pleas of guilt or at trials.

sections.label: Unexplained wealth onus
sections.summary: If a public servant has unexplained wealth, the onus is on that person to prove.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: If you have wealth, you are a public servant, you have wealth which is not explained, the onus is on you to prove.

sections.label: SPF applicant acceptance rate
sections.summary: Fewer than one in ten applicants to SPF is accepted as direct Sergeants or Inspectors.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Less than one out of every 10 applicants to SPF is accepted as direct Sergeants or Inspectors.

sections.label: Women in SPF
sections.summary: SPF has 1,800 women, making up 20%, one-fifth of the force.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Today, we have 1,800 women in SPF making up 20%, one-fifth of the force.

sections.label: Gender no barrier in Police
sections.summary: Gender is no barrier in the Police force, even for physically and mentally demanding roles like the ERT.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Gender is no barrier in the Police force even for the physically and mentally demanding roles like the ERT.

sections.label: Career path to CID Director
sections.summary: A career from Investigation Officer in Operations through various positions to Director of CID at age 42.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Started as Investigation Officer (IO) in Operations, moved on to various positions, then Commander, G Division, spent some time in policy work in MHA, then Director of Operations and now Director in Criminal Investigation Division (CID), which is one of the most senior positions in SPF, at the age of 42.

sections.label: US officer firearm casualties data
sections.summary: A non-profit's data shows 346 officers killed or injured by firearms in the USA in 2020, with resignations up 18%.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: According to data collected by one of the non-profits, number of officers killed or injured by firearms in the USA, 346 last year, in 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Resignations are up 18% from a year ago.

sections.label: Criminal investigations and prosecutions
sections.summary: There were five criminal investigations and, I think, five unsuccessful prosecutions.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Five criminal investigations and, I think, five unsuccessful prosecutions.

sections.label: SPF engagement and manpower
sections.summary: SPF engagement scores rose from 76% in 2018 to 78% last year, and SPF manpower is lean compared to other major cities.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Average scores for engagement across SPF has increased from 76% in 2018, to 78% last year.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Half-yearly, surveys conducted over the last three years consistently showed that more than four out of five SPF officers found their work to be meaningful.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Members will know, SPF's manpower strength is very lean compared to police forces in other major cities such as London, New York and Hong Kong.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: There is a limit to how much our officers can do with the resources that they have.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: We are studying this closely and we will come back on this.

sections.label: Police Bicentennial 2020 Medal
sections.summary: A Singapore Police Bicentennial 2020 Medal will be awarded to SPF officers in service during 2020, with a Medallion for former officers and families of fallen officers.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: A commemorative Singapore Police Bicentennial 2020 Medal will be awarded to SPF officers who were in service for any period between 1 January 2020 and 31 December 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The medal will be worn on their uniform.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: We will also award a Medallion to former Police officers who had retired or completed their National Service liabilities before 1 January 2020, to recognise their contributions.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The families of SPF officers who had given their lives in the line of duty will also receive the Medallion in honour of their contributions and sacrifice.

sections.label: Police Cameras installed since 2012
sections.summary: More than 90,000 Police Cameras have been installed since 2012, and sensor networks will continue to be enhanced.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: In particular, we will continue to enhance our sensor networks.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: We have installed more than 90,000 Police Cameras since 2012, as I have told this House a number of times.

sections.label: Moneylender robbery arrest
sections.summary: A man who robbed a Jurong moneylender of more than $24,000 was identified and arrested within five hours using cameras and investigative techniques.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Visited a moneylender in Jurong, told staff to hand over the cash as he had a firearm, made away with more than $24,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: With the help of cameras and other tech and investigative techniques, he was identified, traced, tracked and arrested in a safe manner within five hours.

sections.label: 200,000 Police Cameras by 2030
sections.summary: The aim is to have at least 200,000 Police Cameras by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: As I have told Members, we aim to have 200,000 Police Cameras, at least, by 2030.

sections.label: Community watch initiatives
sections.summary: Key initiatives include the Safety and Security Watch Group and the upcoming Community Watch Scheme, which will use interest-based community engagement.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Some key initiatives include the Safety and Security Watch Group and the upcoming Community Watch Scheme, which will go beyond geographical-based approaches to interest-based engagements with the community.

sections.label: Singapore Police Bicentennial Medal support
sections.summary: The speaker supports introducing the Singapore Police Bicentennial 2020 Medal and Medallion to honour SPF officers' contributions on its bicentennial.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: And long may this continue for many generations to come.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
sentences.text: I fully support the introduction of the Singapore Police Bicentennial 2020 Medal and Medallion for Police officers and other officers serving with SPF to honour SPF's contributions on the occasion of its bicentennial.

sections.label: Motion for SPF bicentennial
sections.summary: The speaker says the Motion was proposed to commemorate SPF's 200th anniversary, noting CNB formed in 1971 and ICA consolidated in 2003.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
sentences.text: The reason for that, really, is when Mr Murali and I proposed this Motion, it was to commemorate SPF's 200th anniversary, its bicentennial.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
sentences.text: I did a check: CNB was formed in 1971 and ICA was consolidated into the ICA in 2003.

sections.label: Honouring Singapore Police Force contributions
sections.summary: The speaker invites the House to resolve to commemorate SPF's contributions to nation building and keeping Singapore safe.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
sentences.text: As we look to the next 200 years, I am glad to hear from the Minister for Home Affairs that SPF is already enhancing its capabilities to meet the emerging challenges.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
sentences.text: If this is achieved, I am sure that SPF will continue to grow from strength to strength and Singaporeans will get to enjoy many more years of safety and security.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
sentences.text: Therefore, in conclusion, Madam, I invite this House to resolve to commemorate and honour the important contributions of the Singapore Police Force and its officers to nation building and to keeping Singapore as one of the safest countries in the world.
